audi_s7.summary: Autotrader.ca lists the 2024 S7 Sportback in Canada with a 2.9 TFSI six-cylinder rated 444 hp and 442 lb-ft, an automatic gearbox and all-wheel drive, and AutoDeal Canada specifies the automatic as an 8-speed. Reviewers praise the styling, the quality cabin and the hatchback's cargo room, but mention tight rear headroom and a noticeable lag pulling away from a stop. Audi service bulletins covering the S7 deal with 48V mild-hybrid electrical faults and coolant leaks from the V6 TFSI coolant pump. NHTSA lists the 2024 S7 as not crash-rated, and one US recall, for rear-camera software, is on record for the 2024 model year.

issues.issue: 48V mild-hybrid electrical fault: the battery can drain until power is lost; replacing the starter-generator does not fix it.

sources.says: Audi TSB 2073284/1 (9 Mar 2024): electrical fault in the cluster, risk of power loss; root cause is often other CAN-bus sensor faults
Audi TSB 2058831/6 (23 Mar 2023): 48V system warning with DTC P0CA700/U046900 on S7 2020-2023

issues.issue: Coolant leaks from the V6 TFSI coolant pump; the coolant can reach the N649 switch valve and log P0299 underboost.

sources.says: Audi TSB 2070349/4 (30 Aug 2024) for S7 2020-2024: coolant loss, coolant and engine lamps; the pump is the source
parts seller lists the 2019+ C8 S7 2.9T; the pump leaks internally into the vacuum system; Audi has a revised pump
lists the V6 TFSI coolant-pump TSB for the 2021 Audi S7 (NHTSA TSB 10247198, 12 Dec 2023)

issues.issue: Recall: a software fault can stop the rear-camera image appearing in reverse; dealers update the software free.

sources.says: 1 recall for the 2024 S7: 25V900000, rear camera image may not display; dealer software update
Transport Canada returns recall 2025713 (19 Dec 2025) for a 2024 Audi S7 query; its summary describes the rear camera software fault

issues.issue: Noticeable lag pulling away from a stop and occasional jerky low-speed gear changes from the turbo V6 and 8-speed automatic.
issues.years: 2020-2024 (reviews of 2021 and 2024 cars; a 2020 owner in Canada)

sources.says: 2021 S7: occasional throttle lag and jerky low-speed gear changes noted as drawbacks
2024 S7 test car: noticeable lag from a stop or after a downshift makes it feel jerky
a 2020 S7 at about 60,000 km in Canada shows a noticeable delay when accelerating; no replies or fix

issues.issue: Earlier C8 S7s carry many recalls: ten NHTSA campaigns list the 2021 S7, from seat-belt retractors to instrument-display software.

sources.says: Count 10, incl. 21V295000 rear trailing-arm lock nut, 22V155000 fuel level sender, 25V201000 instrument display software

mods.mod: APR ECU software upgrade (Stage 1) for the 2.9T EA839, flashed through the OBD-II port
mods.why: More power and torque across the rev range; an S7 C8 owner says it made a large difference

sources.says: S7 C8 owner runs the APR tune and says it made a big difference; links APR's EA839 C8 software
Canadian shop lists the APR ECU upgrade for the S7 (C8): OBD-port flash, several octane files, E60-E85 support

mods.caveat: WCT's listing offers 'APR Plus', described as a limited powertrain warranty matched to the factory term; it says nothing on emissions legality.

mods.mod: Air suspension controller (CETE) to lower or raise the car per Drive Select mode
mods.why: Use the full range of the factory air suspension, with set heights per mode and by speed, and a 'show mode' low setting

sources.says: vendor post: CETE controller for C8 A6/S6/A7/S7 with factory air suspension, app-controlled, per-mode and speed settings
a 2020 C8 S6 build lists a CETE suspension module (S6 and S7 share the APR file and the Audi TSBs)

mods.mod: Bolt-ons on one C8 S6 build: aftermarket intake, resonator delete, forged 21x10 wheels, front lip and RS-style grille
mods.why: Sound (the owner posted clips of the resonator delete) and looks; the owner gives no other reason

sources.says: 2020 S6: APR Stage 1 on 93 octane, Roc Euro intake, resonator delete, BC Forged 21x10 wheels, OBD11 flashing tool

bentley_flying_spur_2018.summary: Reviewers of this generation praise the build quality, the cabin materials and the effortless, smooth V8, and the RAC calls the car very reliable. The criticisms are a ride that is less smooth than expected, light and vague steering with plenty of body roll, a heavy car, and sat-nav and technology that trail the Mercedes S-Class (evo, 2014). Fuel use and running costs are the common complaint: The Car Guide lists fuel consumption as its con and the RAC scores running costs 3/10. On the repair side, Bentley's own bulletins cover leaking air springs and turbocharger damage caused by a clogged oil strainer on the V8. NHTSA lists no owner complaints filed for the 2018 Flying Spur.

issues.issue: Air springs (air suspension struts) leak, so a corner sags or the suspension faults; Bentley issued a fault-finding procedure for it.
issues.years: 2014-2018 Flying Spur per the Bentley bulletin; Continental and Flying Spur generally per the parts supplier

sources.says: Bentley technical product information 2030217/5 'Air spring fault finding' lists leaking shock absorbers/air springs at each corner and covers Flying Spur model years 2014-2018 (filed with NHTSA)

a UK Bentley parts supplier says air leaking from the damper is the most common Continental GT/Flying Spur suspension fault it sees; bellows dry out and tear with age (promotional page, no years given)
a buying guide for the 2020-on Flying Spur says leaking air chambers that overwork the pump affect Flying Spurs past and present

issues.issue: Turbocharger damage and hard starting when carbon clogs the oil strainer feeding the turbos; Bentley fitted a larger strainer.

sources.says: Bentley TSB 2052085/2 (May 2019), V8 4.0TFSI: hard starting, noise and low power from damaged turbos; carbon and soot build up in the turbo oil strainer; repair replaces both turbos plus the strainer and non-return valve

issues.issue: Front anti-roll bar drop links wear and start to knock.

sources.says: the front anti-roll bar drop links often wear and knock (about GBP 50 each); the variable dampers rarely give trouble

issues.issue: Tyre-pressure sensor batteries run out at about five years, and the sensors are costly to replace.

sources.says: the tyre-pressure sensors' built-in batteries die at around five years; about GBP 142 each, around GBP 900 plus VAT with fitting

bmw_i8_2016.summary: Cars.com's review, written for the 2015 car and stated to apply to the largely unchanged 2016, praises the supercar styling, brisk acceleration, efficiency against exotic rivals and interior quality, but finds the car heavy-feeling, hard to get into and out of, and short on rear-seat room. CarGurus credits strong performance and efficiency for the price but criticises a firm ride, numb electric steering, poor rear visibility and little luggage space. Owners in a Rennlist thread like the looks, the instant electric torque and the comfortable highway cruising, but dislike the piped-in engine sound and an electric range of roughly 21 miles. BMW service bulletins for the 2016 car concern the drive electronics (EME) and the fuel filler flap, owners report costly electric A/C compressor failures, and a UK used-car guide calls total high-voltage battery failures rare.

issues.issue: Drive electronics (EME) faults bring up a 'Drivetrain fault' message or engine light; fixes range from software to EME replacement.

sources.says: TSB B122815: 'Drivetrain fault' message with EME drive-position and parking-lock codes, caused by EME software
TSB B122215: intermittent engine light with an inverter current-sensor code, caused by an EME software error
TSB B612916: engine light from an internal EME fault; remedy is replacing the EME

issues.issue: Fuel filler flap can fail to unlock or set a 'Fuel tank system faulty' message.
issues.years: 2016 (bulletin); the UK guide does not split by year

sources.says: TSB B511715: the filler-flap locking rod disconnects from central locking, storing a jammed-button code
the flap can fail to unlock, more often on hot days; the fix may mean a pressure sensor and dropping the tank

issues.issue: Electric A/C compressor can fail internally and spread metal debris through the refrigerant circuit that also cools the battery.
issues.years: i8 generally; sources do not single out a year

sources.says: the i8's battery is refrigerant-cooled, and owners have reported compressor failures with metal in the lines
owners warn a failing compressor can contaminate the cooling circuit; full repair put near 15,000 euros

issues.issue: High-voltage battery: total failures described as rare and wear as low, but ask for a recent battery health check.
issues.years: all I12 i8s (the 2018 update brought a larger pack)

sources.says: liquid-cooled lithium-ion pack from the i3; total failures are rare
owners near 200,000 km report under 10% capacity loss; get a recent battery diagnostic before buying

issues.issue: Rear window heater elements can fail.
issues.years: 2014-2020 per the guide (not split by year)

sources.says: rear glass heater elements can fail, usually sorted under warranty

issues.issue: Turbocharger coolant-pump signal fault sets a 'Drive Check' message while the car drives normally.

sources.says: TSB B170215: fault code for an implausible turbo coolant pump signal, no drivability problem

mods.mod: Lowering springs (AC Schnitzer and H&R named), sometimes with extra negative camber.
mods.why: Flatter cornering and a sharper front end, with the ride said to stay pliant when cruising; also stance.

sources.says: Schnitzer springs drop the car 25 mm front, 20 mm rear; livelier handling, ride hard to tell from stock
H&R springs lower the car 0.75 in front and 0.6 in rear, with BMW upper A-arms for camber

mods.mod: Aftermarket forged or larger wheels (AC Schnitzer, Forgeline and Savini named).
mods.why: Lower weight and looks; one forged set was about 4.4 kg lighter than stock despite being bigger.

sources.says: AC1 forged wheels about 4.4 kg lighter overall, on wider Michelin Pilot Super Sport tyres
a build on 22-inch Savini wheels with H&R springs, said to improve stance and ride

mods.mod: Full vinyl wraps over the factory paint.
mods.why: Visual impact; the stock colour stays underneath.

sources.says: a camouflage wrap over a satin black base; a similar design is estimated at $3,000-5,000
a bright yellow wrap fitted by the tuner

mods.mod: Carbon-fibre aero and body kits (spoilers, canards, diffuser, wing).
mods.why: Looks; the reviewer felt most parts suit the car but the rear wing looks out of place.

sources.says: full AC Schnitzer conversion quoted at 34,995 pounds excluding wrap; large carbon parts over 3,000 pounds each
a UK i8 with a velvet wrap and carbon add-ons was ticketed by police

mods.caveat: Police in Manchester ticketed one modified i8 for bodywork add-ons judged likely to cause injury (and a cracked windscreen).

mods.mod: Aftermarket titanium exhaust.
mods.why: The stock car is quiet and much of the cabin sound is piped in; owners want real exhaust noise and less weight.

sources.says: an Arqray titanium exhaust weighs 18 lb vs 36 lb stock and adds pops on lift-off; fitting needs undertrays removed
a titanium exhaust about 50% lighter makes the car much louder from outside

mods.mod: Switching off the Active Sound Design (the synthetic engine sound).
mods.why: Owners find the piped-in sound fake; BMW gives no setting to turn it off.

sources.says: no factory switch, but the car can be modified to remove it; the three-cylinder sounds better than expected
owners call the piped-in engine sound fake and unpleasant

mods.mod: Apple CarPlay added through an aftermarket interface box.
mods.why: Some owners see the stock infotainment as basic; the box needs no coding and is reversible.

sources.says: an owner fitted a CarPlay box in about 4.5 hours, hidden under the glovebox, with no software change

mods.mod: Fitting the later, larger 11.7 kWh high-voltage battery to a pre-2018 car (discussed, rarely worth it).
mods.why: More electric range, but posters say it adds only about 10-12 km and call it uneconomic.

sources.says: reportedly dealer-only work estimated at 15,000-20,000 euros; replacing a healthy pack is not economical

mods.caveat: Posters say the 8-year/100,000 km battery warranty may be refused if scheduled maintenance was missed or charge capacity is low.

porsche_911_c4_2012.summary: A Canadian test of the 2012 Carrera 4, the last of the 997 line, praised its all-wheel-drive grip on snow and ice and the long options list; its one stated drawback was keeping the 997 styling just as the 991 arrived, and Auto123 likewise pitched the Carrera 4 as a Porsche suited to Canada. The Car Guide scores the 2012 911 10/10 for driving and safety and 8/10 for reliability, and lists high prices, costly options, running costs and limited cargo space as its cons. Owners on CarGurus praise the handling, power and timeless looks but note limited space, cabin noise at speed and rear seats fit only for children. Specialists say the 9A1 engine has no IMS bearing and is less prone to bore scoring than the 997.1, though cold-start piston seizures are still reported, and owner forums name the water pump, air-oil separator and high-pressure fuel pump as the usual repair items.

issues.issue: Cylinder bore scoring or piston seizure: still possible on the 9A1, but reported far less often than on the 997.1.

sources.says: bore-scoring risk drops on the 997.2 but is not zero; confirm suspect noises with a borescope
cylinder scoring and seizing is the one main 9A1 Gen 2 failure the shop reports, described as very minor

issues.issue: Cold seizure: the lower bore warms slowly, so hard driving before full warm-up can seize a piston.

sources.says: the 9A1 lower bore expands more slowly than older engines, so allow longer warm-up before high revs
the documented seized engines reportedly all failed in winter after short, fast drives from cold

rolls_royce_ghost_2014.summary: Reviewers praise the deep soundproofing, the lavish interior and its leatherwork, the strong V12 and the smooth eight-speed gearbox, and the comfort on smooth roads. The criticisms are steering that is light and inert, a car that feels big and heavy, body lean and a nose that rises under hard acceleration, a ride that loosens at high speed and large wheels that thump over potholes; The Car Guide also lists low resale value as a con. The few owners who rated the 2014 car on Cars.com give it 5/5, with reliability at 4.7/5. Used-car guides to this generation tell buyers to check for failing injectors, carbon build-up, oil and coolant leaks, air suspension faults and water getting into the cabin. NHTSA lists no owner complaints for the 2014 Ghost.

rolls_royce_wraith_2017.summary: Reviewers praise the 624 bhp twin-turbo V12, which makes the Wraith the fastest Rolls-Royce of its time, along with a very quiet cabin and the materials and craftsmanship inside. The criticisms are light steering with little feedback, a car that is not really a driver's car, poor visibility, a narrow boot and a ride that suffers at speed; evo felt the BMW-derived infotainment dilutes the hand-built feel, though the RAC rated its controller among the best. Running costs and value score lowest with the RAC, and Auto Express felt it does not quite justify its price. Used guides tell buyers to check the injectors, carbon build-up, oil and coolant pipes and the air suspension, while PistonHeads (2024) calls the V12 solid but thirsty. The two Cars.com owners rate it 5/5, and NHTSA lists no owner complaints for the 2017 model year.
